entries.verdict_line: Iron ore at $161.91 — a 65% single-session surge to a 63rd-percentile print — is either the most important China stimulus signal of 2026 or the most dangerous head-fake for India's capex narrative.
Airline passengers down 9.1% MoM to a 7th-percentile low while GST prints ₹2.01 lakh crore — India's consumption story has two floors, and the one carrying the weight just cracked.
SIP inflows slipped to ₹29,845 cr while FII equity net flipped to -₹114 cr — domestic liquidity is still the floor, but it just got thinner.
Nikkei at a 100th-percentile high while printing 6,681 — a data anomaly or the sharpest single-session dislocation in a decade — and Bank Nifty's 94th-percentile perch looks lonelier by the hour.
Natural gas at $3.01 — an 18th-percentile distress print — is the one commodity telling the truth about global demand while copper and iron ore perform their China stimulus pantomime.
India VIX at a 7th-percentile low while FII equity net flips to -₹114 cr — the market is pricing serenity precisely when the smart money is quietly leaving the room.
PMI Services at 57.5 — an 88th-percentile print — is sliding fast enough that the composite's 86th-percentile glow may be last quarter's story by September.
Gold at ₹12,520/gram — a 100th-percentile INR print — while copper climbs and oil creeps: India's commodity import bill is quietly repricing before anyone has updated their CAD models.

Airline passengers collapsed 9.1% MoM to a 7th-percentile low while vehicle sales surged 26% — India's consumption story has split in two, and only one half is real.
SIP accounts at a 2nd-percentile low while AUM hits ₹16.64 lakh cr — India's equity cult is deepening among the wealthy and quietly abandoning the mass investor.
Euro Stoxx 50 at a 10-year high while US GDP prints 0.7% SAAR — global equities are pricing a soft landing that the underlying economy has already left behind.
Nikkei at a 10-year high yet down 4% in two sessions — global carry trades are unwinding, and India's ₹96.15 INR hasn't blinked yet.
S&P 500 at a 100th-percentile high yet down 1.5% in a session — global risk appetite is cracking precisely when India's FII flows swung from +₹22,615 cr to -₹114 cr.
Nikkei down 4% in two sessions from a 10-year high — the carry trade is unwinding in Tokyo, and India's INR at 96.15 hasn't moved yet.
WTI up $3.5 in six weeks to $82.58 while US GDP prints 0.7% SAAR — oil is pricing a demand that the world's largest economy has already stopped producing.
Copper up 3.7% in a session while US PMI prints 50.3 — industrial metals are pricing a recovery that the world's largest economy has already stopped delivering.
Airline passenger traffic at a 7th-percentile low while vehicle sales surge 26% — India's consumption story is bifurcating, and the weaker half is the one that travels.
US 10Y at 4.67% — an 84th-percentile print — is repricing global carry trades while India's Bank Nifty sits at a 93rd-percentile high on a funding structure that cannot survive the spillover.
SIP accounts grew just 1.6% — a 2nd-percentile crawl — while inflows hit ₹29,845 cr; India's retail equity story is deepening, not widening, and that distinction matters for the next correction.
US 10Y at 4.71% — a 4-of-5 rising streak — is the rate that breaks India's carry arithmetic, yet India VIX at a 9th-percentile low says nobody has priced it.
Nikkei at a 100th-percentile high sheds 2.7% in a session — Tokyo's unwind is the canary; India's VIX at a 9th-percentile low says the cage door is still open.
Natural gas at a 16th-percentile low while iron ore jumps 21% — global commodity markets are sending contradictory demand signals, and India's import bill is caught in the crossfire.
PMI Services at an 88th-percentile high while e-commerce GMV growth halved to 12.4% — India's service economy is thriving for the affluent and stalling for everyone else.
US GDP at 0.7% SAAR while S&P 500 hits a 100th-percentile high — the gap between price and growth is the widest since the 2021 liquidity bubble, and copper at $6.37 says the real economy disagrees.
Airline passengers fell 9% MoM to a 7th-percentile low while PV sales surged 26.1% — India's consumption story is bifurcating, and the fault line runs straight through the middle class.

US 10Y at 4.68% — an 84th-percentile print while US GDP prints 0.7% SAAR — means the world's risk-free rate is priced for growth that no longer exists.
